summary.headline: The Community Preservation Committee reviewed major updates for Fayville Park, Peninsula Trail Phase 2, and preparations for its June public forum.
summary.summary: The Community Preservation Committee met to receive project updates regarding the Audubon International management plan at the Southborough Golf Club and public feedback on the Fayville Memorial Park proposal, including parking and splash pad placement. The committee also evaluated the Phase 1 closeout and potential Phase 2 scope for the Peninsula Trail, which faces escalating construction costs. Members reviewed standard CPA project signage and updated their presentation slides for the annual public forum, which was scheduled for June 11, 2026.

topics.title: Audubon International golf course management plan
topics.summary: Representatives from the Golf Course Committee and Open Space Preservation Commission provided an update on drafting a request for proposals to hire a consultant for the Audubon International certification management plan. The consultant will establish environmental guidelines for managing and maintaining the Southborough Golf Club.
key_details: The RFP is being drafted with assistance from the Conservation Commission.
The Golf Course Committee expects to review the outline in early June.
The committee aims to award the contract and begin work by mid-June 2026.
The management framework is intended to be in place prior to construction work on the golf course irrigation project.
topics.outcome: Draft RFP requirements will be finalized with the Conservation Commission and reviewed by the Golf Course Committee.

topics.title: Fayville Memorial Park redesign and parking updates
topics.summary: Recreation department officials shared community feedback on proposed renovations to Fayville Memorial Park following two public forums and outreach at Touch-a-Truck. Discussions focused heavily on resolving neighborhood parking concerns and finalizing park layout options.
key_details: Public feedback favored a design placing the splash pad adjacent to the playground rather than in the center, preserving green space and winter sledding areas.
The splash pad footprint has been reduced from an initial 8,000 square feet to 2,000 square feet.
A formal parking study conducted with landscape architect Activitas is expected within a week to assess street parking along Central Street and options near Fayville Hall.
Recreation officials are seeking a Land and Water Conservation Fund grant that could reimburse up to 50 percent of eligible project costs.
A finalized revised CPC application with precise parking counts and project costs is due by June 30, 2026.
topics.outcome: The Recreation Commission will finalize parking options and submit a revised application by the June 30 deadline.
topics.why_it_matters: The project represents a substantial town park renovation requiring significant CPA and grant funding while addressing neighborhood safety and parking capacity.

topics.title: Rural Cemetery tower and golf irrigation updates
topics.summary: The chair gave brief updates on the status of projects involving the Rural Cemetery water tower restoration and the Southborough Golf Club irrigation system. Both project proponents plan to attend the next committee meeting with further details.
key_details: Rural Cemetery representatives are exploring project alternatives and coordinating with the Select Board.
Golf course officials are evaluating whether revolving fund revenues can offset a portion of irrigation project costs.
topics.outcome: Both project sponsors are scheduled to present updates at the committee's June meeting.

topics.title: Peninsula Trail Phase 1 closeout and Phase 2 scope
topics.summary: The Trails Committee discussed the closeout of Peninsula Trail Phase 1 and options for Phase 2 construction across wetlands. Phase 2 costs have risen significantly, prompting discussion about whether to build both a bridge and a boardwalk or scale back to a bridge with an upland workaround trail.
key_details: Phase 1 has roughly $40,000 in unspent funds that will be returned to the general CPA fund balance upon closeout.
Prior contractor bids for the combined bridge and boardwalk came in between $427,600 and $448,000, which with inflation and contingencies could exceed $600,000.
Phase 2 currently has $211,000 allocated, leaving a potential funding gap of over $350,000 for the full design.
Trails Committee volunteers have scheduled trail work in June to explore an upland walking route around the wetland as an alternative to the boardwalk.
Committee members discussed whether the Department of Public Works or the Town Engineer should assist volunteer boards with technical project oversight.
topics.outcome: The Trails Committee will consult its full membership on project scope and return to the CPC with recommended next steps.
topics.why_it_matters: Funding the full Phase 2 trail design could require asking Town Meeting for hundreds of thousands of dollars in additional funding or settling for a less accessible upland trail.

topics.title: Standardized CPA project signage
topics.summary: The committee reviewed sample templates and vendor quotes to establish standardized recognition signs for CPA-funded town projects. Members discussed sign dimensions, post materials, and whether to order blanks in bulk from Signarama.
key_details: Signarama estimated a cost of approximately $100 per 12-by-16-inch PVC sign.
The committee considered purchasing five to ten standard blanks to reduce per-unit costs.
Members agreed to review physical sign size samples and post pricing before placing an order.
topics.outcome: Members will inspect size samples and review post options at an upcoming meeting.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The committee reviewed draft meeting minutes from February 26, 2026, and March 26, 2026. The February minutes were tabled for clarification on attendance and votes, while the March minutes were approved.
key_details: Action on the February 26, 2026 minutes was postponed to allow members to verify attendance records.
The committee approved the March 26, 2026 meeting minutes as amended.
topics.outcome: March 26, 2026 minutes were approved; February 26, 2026 minutes were tabled.

topics.title: Annual Public Forum presentation and date setting
topics.summary: Members walked through the slide deck for the upcoming annual CPA public forum. The committee updated financial figures to reflect the latest tax rate, surcharge estimates, reserve balances, and completed project lists, and agreed on a date for the forum.
key_details: Based on an average single-family home value of $957,500 and a tax rate of $14.36 per thousand, the average annual CPA surcharge is estimated at $127.95.
The presentation clarifies that recreation projects are funded from the undesignated or general unreserved CPA fund balance rather than a dedicated statutory bucket.
The committee selected Thursday, June 11, 2026, at 7:00 PM for the annual public forum.
topics.outcome: The presentation slides will be revised and posted online ahead of the public forum on June 11, 2026.
